data.narrative:
Climeworks is a Series F–stage climate and energy company that has raised over $1.0B to date. The comparable universe in Climate & Energy comprises 9 peers: one public company (Linea Acquisition Corp., LNZA) and eight private firms including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen at various development and funding stages.

Valuation analysis relied on stage-progression methodology, as peer-median triangulation was not applicable. The Climate & Energy sector contained insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum statistical thresholds (fewer than three datapoints in narrow peer filters). The stage-progression method applied a 1.3x multiplier typical of Series F advancement to the $1.0B total-raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $1.3B.

Analysis supports a valuation range of $1.1B (low) to $1.5B (high), with a median point of $1.3B. This range reflects limited triangulation depth; reliance on a single method introduces material uncertainty around the point estimate. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 1.3x stage multiplier for this specific company, the representativeness of total raised as a valuation proxy, and the heterogeneity of the broader Climate & Energy peer set. The lack of tightly comparable private transactions at Series F stage constrains confidence in the derivation.
